newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility extreme in Zitel slide.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility extreme in Zitel slide.

text.p: Volatility in Zitel Corp options remained extreme as the stock slumped after rallying sharply in early activity, traders said Monday.
"They're still to the moon," one trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said, referring to volatilities on Zitel options.
Zitel shares rallied early Monday to an all-time high of 72-7/8 but began an afternoon slide that gathered steam as the session wore on.
The stock eventually finished down 20-1/4 points at 41. Volume topped 11.1 million shares.
Implied volatility for the January 60 calls was around 170 on the bid, 188 on the offer in afternoon trade, traders said.
The stock's historical volatility was around 98.
At the end of last week, implied volatility in some of the active options was already high at around 141.
Zitel shares had rallied straight from around 30 in seven trading sessions.
Analysts pegged the rise to a short squeeze, rumored buying by investor George Soros and optimism about the company's involvement in finding a solution for the so-called Year 2000 computer bug.
A source close to Soros Fund Management told Reuters Monday that Soros did not own any Zitel shares and did not plan to buy any.
The stock's volatility Monday kept implied volatilities in the options steep.
"These volatilities are crazy," the broker said. "They are not something to take lightly as a premium buyer."
But he added that they made being a premium seller a difficult task as well.
The trader at the CBOE said activity was strong from both retail and institutional investors.
"There's a little bit of everything going on," he said, adding that when the stock began to drop from its highs, investors began to sell calls into the drop.
According to data from McMillan Analysis Corp, Zitel options volume last Friday rose to nearly 14,000 contracts, from a daily average of roughly 4,200.
The busiest Zitel options included the January 65 call, which traded about 4,560 contracts, and the January 60 call, which traded roughly 3,855.
Among the puts, the January 50 traded 1,675 and the January 60 traded 1,595 contracts.
The January 50 put rose 7-3/4 to 11-1/2 after dropping early to 2-5/16..

The broker noted that even some deep out-of-the-money puts, such as the 35s, which need the stock to drop below that level to become valuable, were relatively expensive and had high implied volatility.
The January 35 put ended at 3-3/4, up 2-7/8, on volume of more than 450 contracts.
"These are probably some of the most expensive puts I've seen in a long time," he said. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com))
